content.content:
1	---
2	name: windows-parallel-agents
3	description: Windows-safe protocol for dispatching parallel Claude Code subagents with git worktree isolation. Use any time the orchestrator needs to run 2+ agents in parallel on Windows, or any time the Agent tool's isolation="worktree" parameter is being considered. Trigger phrases include "dispatch parallel agents", "run agents in parallel", "parallel wave", "parallel dispatch", "isolation: worktree", "create worktrees", "windows worktree", "multiple agents at once", "agents in parallel". Prevents cross-agent file leakage, missed commits, and the sibling-worktree data-loss class of bugs common on native Windows.
4	---
5	
6	# Windows Parallel Agent Dispatch Protocol — v3
7	
8	Use this skill any time you are about to launch **2 or more agents in parallel** while developing on Windows. It prevents three classes of failure we hit in Sprint 002 Waves 1–2:
9	
10	1. **Cross-agent file leakage** — agents writing to the main repo instead of their worktree.
11	2. **Missed commits** — agents leaving work uncommitted, forcing the orchestrator to go into each worktree and commit by hand.
12	3. **Sibling-worktree contamination** — agent writes into another agent's worktree (rare, but non-recoverable when it happens; added protection in v3 after GitHub issue #41010 surfaced a data-loss variant).
13	
14	## Why Claude Code's `isolation: "worktree"` is broken on Windows
15	
16	The harness creates the worktree directory correctly but does **not** rewrite the sub-agent's `<env>Working directory:</env>` context line. On Windows, agents read that line, use absolute paths derived from it (which point to main), and their writes land in the main repo instead of the worktree.
17	
18	### Known-broken scenarios (confirmed via GitHub issues, unfixed as of v2.1.72)
19	
20	| Issue  | Scenario                                                      | Outcome                                               |
21	| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
22	| #40164 | `isolation: "worktree"` on Windows 11                         | Path-resolution mismatch; falls back to main silently |
23	| #39886 | `isolation: "worktree"` alone                                 | Worktree never created; agent runs in main            |
24	| #37549 | `isolation: "worktree"` + `team_name` (agent teams)           | Silently fails; agent runs in main                    |
25	| #33045 | `isolation: "worktree"` + `team_name` (different repro)       | No effect; agent runs in main                         |
26	| #41010 | Sub-agent ID collides with parent worktree name               | Cleanup deletes parent's working dir — DATA LOSS      |
27	| #39680 | `.claude/worktrees/` already exists                           | EEXIST error on Linux/macOS                           |
28	| #34645 | Multiple parallel subagents creating worktrees simultaneously | `git config` lock contention                          |
29	
30	Linux / macOS don't see most of these — different shell-spawning internals and filesystem semantics.
31	
32	**Do not use the Agent tool's `isolation: "worktree"` parameter on this machine.** Pre-create worktrees manually instead.
33	
34	**Note on `claude --worktree`:** Claude Code v2.1.49 (Feb 19, 2026) added a native `--worktree` flag, and v2.1.72+ added the `ExitWorktree` tool. These help when you're launching a _single_ Claude Code session into a worktree. They do NOT fix the parallel-subagent case, which is what this skill addresses.
35

---
name: windows-parallel-agents
description: Windows-safe protocol for dispatching parallel Claude Code subagents with git worktree isolation. Use any time the orchestrator needs to run 2+ agents in parallel on Windows, or any time the Agent tool's isolation="worktree" parameter is being considered. Trigger phrases include "dispatch parallel agents", "run agents in parallel", "parallel wave", "parallel dispatch", "isolation: worktree", "create worktrees", "windows worktree", "multiple agents at once", "agents in parallel". Prevents cross-agent file leakage, missed commits, and the sibling-worktree data-loss class of bugs common on native Windows.
---

# Windows Parallel Agent Dispatch Protocol — v3

Use this skill any time you are about to launch **2 or more agents in parallel** while developing on Windows. It prevents three classes of failure we hit in Sprint 002 Waves 1–2:

1. **Cross-agent file leakage** — agents writing to the main repo instead of their worktree.
2. **Missed commits** — agents leaving work uncommitted, forcing the orchestrator to go into each worktree and commit by hand.
3. **Sibling-worktree contamination** — agent writes into another agent's worktree (rare, but non-recoverable when it happens; added protection in v3 after GitHub issue #41010 surfaced a data-loss variant).

## Why Claude Code's `isolation: "worktree"` is broken on Windows

The harness creates the worktree directory correctly but does **not** rewrite the sub-agent's `<env>Working directory:</env>` context line. On Windows, agents read that line, use absolute paths derived from it (which point to main), and their writes land in the main repo instead of the worktree.

### Known-broken scenarios (confirmed via GitHub issues, unfixed as of v2.1.72)

| Issue  | Scenario                                                      | Outcome                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| #40164 | `isolation: "worktree"` on Windows 11                         | Path-resolution mismatch; falls back to main silently |
| #39886 | `isolation: "worktree"` alone                                 | Worktree never created; agent runs in main            |
| #37549 | `isolation: "worktree"` + `team_name` (agent teams)           | Silently fails; agent runs in main                    |
| #33045 | `isolation: "worktree"` + `team_name` (different repro)       | No effect; agent runs in main                         |
| #41010 | Sub-agent ID collides with parent worktree name               | Cleanup deletes parent's working dir — DATA LOSS      |
| #39680 | `.claude/worktrees/` already exists                           | EEXIST error on Linux/macOS                           |
| #34645 | Multiple parallel subagents creating worktrees simultaneously | `git config` lock contention                          |

Linux / macOS don't see most of these — different shell-spawning internals and filesystem semantics.

**Do not use the Agent tool's `isolation: "worktree"` parameter on this machine.** Pre-create worktrees manually instead.

**Note on `claude --worktree`:** Claude Code v2.1.49 (Feb 19, 2026) added a native `--worktree` flag, and v2.1.72+ added the `ExitWorktree` tool. These help when you're launching a _single_ Claude Code session into a worktree. They do NOT fix the parallel-subagent case, which is what this skill addresses.

## The protocol (orchestrator's steps)

1. **Pre-install shared deps on main, in one commit** before the wave. Every agent that needs a new dependency installs it via one orchestrator-led commit; agents never touch package.json. This removes the biggest source of parallel merge conflicts.

2. **Pre-create one worktree per agent**: `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<agent-id> -b feat/<agent-id>` from the main repo. Use stable IDs (e.g., `b103-safe-action`) so branch names match backlog items. **Do not use agent IDs whose first 8 characters could collide** with an existing worktree name under `.claude/worktrees/` — this is the #41010 data-loss trigger.

3. **Dispatch each agent with the hardened prompt prefix** from `prompt-template.md` (v3). Substitute **all six** placeholders before sending:
   - `<WORKTREE_PATH>`, `<WORKTREE_PATH_FORWARD_SLASH>`, `<WORKTREE_NAME>`, `<MAIN_REPO_PATH_FORWARD_SLASH>`, `<BRANCH_NAME>`, `<COMMIT_MESSAGE>`.

   Run all agents with `run_in_background: true` so you can monitor.

4. **Monitor while agents run.** Run `git status --short` on main periodically. If it shows anything dirty, an agent leaked. Stash immediately with `git stash push -u -m "WAVE-N-LEAK-QUARANTINE"` to contain the leak so later agents see a clean tree. Investigate after the wave finishes.

5. **After every agent returns**, verify:
   - Agent reported `VERDICT: WORKTREE RESPECTED` (no leak)
   - Agent's first-response re-anchor statement is present (v3 requirement)
   - Write-path assertion output is `OK` (v3 requirement)
   - `git log main..feat/<branch>` shows at least 1 commit (no missed commit)
   - Agent pasted `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` matching the worktree path

6. **Merge sequentially** with `git merge --no-ff --no-edit`. Suggested order:
   1. Infrastructure-only branches (`.github/workflows/**`, runbook docs)
   2. Standalone new-file branches (pure-add, no edits)
   3. Config-edit branches (`eslint.config.mjs`, `next.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`)
   4. Shared-file edit branches (`app/layout.tsx`, `package.json`) — git auto-merges different sections reliably

   Run `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npm run format:check` between merges. Run `npm run format` + one `style(...)` commit if format has drifted.

7. **Cleanup after merge:**
   ```
   git worktree remove --force .claude/worktrees/<agent-id>
   git branch -D feat/<agent-id>
   ```

## Anti-patterns that caused prior leakage

- Agent uses the `<env>Working directory:</env>` line instead of running `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first → writes to main. **v3 mitigation: mandatory re-anchor statement in first response.**
- Agent edits a file in-place that also exists in main, creating a `.bak` backup that lands in main. **v3 mitigation: forbidden-paths block explicitly denies writes outside your worktree.**
- Agent runs `npm install` from a directory that resolves to main's `package.json`. **v3 mitigation: pre-commit CWD sanity check catches this.**
- Agent ends without committing → orchestrator has to chase down each worktree and commit manually. **v3 mitigation: directive commit-or-fail language and explicit husky fallback.**
- Two agents both add dependencies → main's `package.json` + `package-lock.json` get tangled at merge time. **Orchestrator mitigation: install up front (step 1).**
- Agent writes into a sibling agent's worktree because it resolved a relative path from the wrong cwd. **v3 mitigation: forbidden-paths explicitly denies sibling worktree prefix.**
- Sub-agent with colliding 8-char ID prefix cleans up and deletes parent's worktree (#41010). **Orchestrator mitigation: use backlog-linked stable IDs; never nest orchestrator inside a worktree.**

## Sibling files

- **`prompt-template.md`** — exact hardened prefix to prepend to every parallel-agent prompt (v3).
- **`orchestrator-flow.md`** — step-by-step bash-level commands for an N-agent wave end-to-end.

## Validation history

- v1 (baseline): 2/2 test agents (2026-04-15)
- v1 → v2: 9/9 Wave 2 agents, 1 leak caught + corrected (2026-04-15)
- v2: 10/10 Wave 3 agents, 0 leaks, 0 missed commits (2026-04-15) — both gaps closed with v2 hardened prompt
- v2 → v3: [TO VALIDATE ON NEXT WAVE] Research-driven hardening. Adds mandatory re-anchor, write-path assertion, forbidden-paths enforcement, pre-commit sanity check, and husky fallback. Targeted at the #41010 sibling-worktree class of failures that v2 had no protection against.

## Future direction: WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove hooks

Claude Code now supports `WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` hooks. The endgame for this skill is to move validation OUT of the prompt prefix and INTO deterministic hooks:

- The `WorktreeCreate` hook creates the worktree, writes the correct absolute path into a well-known file (e.g., `.claude/current-worktree-path.txt`), and returns the path on stdout.
- The prompt prefix becomes: "Read `.claude/current-worktree-path.txt` as your first action; that is your working directory."
- Path substitution stops being a manual orchestrator chore and becomes a property of the hook.

This is future work. The current v3 prompt-based approach is battle-tested enough to keep shipping with; the hook-based approach requires more infrastructure before it's worth the migration.

## Placeholders (v3 adds two)

- `<WORKTREE_PATH>` — Windows-style absolute path, e.g. `E:\rk-telerads-gas-final\rkt-platform\.claude\worktrees\b123-flags`

- `<WORKTREE_NAME>` — just the final path component, e.g. `b123-flags` **[NEW in v3]**
- `<MAIN_REPO_PATH_FORWARD_SLASH>` — main repo root, forward-slash form, e.g. `E:/rk-telerads-gas-final/rkt-platform` **[NEW in v3]**
- `<BRANCH_NAME>` — e.g. `feat/b123-flags`
- `<COMMIT_MESSAGE>` — the full commit message (subject + body) the agent will use in its mandatory final commit

---

```

content.text:
**Nothing domain-specific — Chandra is a general-purpose OCR model.** Datalab has not published medical-specific fine-tunes or healthcare presets for Chandra.

**What Datalab *does* offer that we can leverage for medical docs:**

1. **`/extract-structured-data` with custom JSON schemas** — you can pass a schema describing medical fields (test_name, value, unit, reference_range). The model is guided by your schema, gets better field-level accuracy, and returns per-field confidence scores. Our clinical JSON schema plugs directly in.

2. **Saved schemas** (`/extraction_schemas/*`) — you create the medical-document schema once, reuse across every lab report, discharge summary, prescription. Also supports confidence thresholds per field.

3. **Custom processors / pipelines** — chain `/convert` → `/extract` with validation rules specific to medical docs (e.g., "reject if patient name missing").

4. **Eval rubrics** — you build rubrics like "did it extract all lab values?" and run them against a batch. Useful for weekly clinical audits.

5. **`block_correction_prompt`** (Marker feature, Chandra-powered) — lets you pass domain hints like "this is a pediatric Indian lab report with metric units."

**No medical fine-tune, no ICD-10 awareness, no SNOMED mapping.** Those remain the Claude Haiku structuring layer's job.

Forge is Datalab's evaluation framework that ships with ready-made benchmark sets — legal is one, but it's a showcase, not a product tier. There is **no medical-document equivalent shipped by Datalab today.**

**What you can do:**

1. **Build your own medical Forge eval** — Datalab lets you create private eval collections + rubrics (the `/eval_rubrics/*` and `/collections/*` endpoints I noted earlier). You feed in ~50 anonymized lab reports / discharge summaries / prescriptions with ground-truth labels, define rubrics ("extracted all lab values?", "got test_date right?", "caught critical flag?"), and Forge runs the pipeline against them every time you change a prompt, schema, or provider. That is exactly what the legal eval demo is — just pointed at your docs.

2. **Publicly available medical OCR benchmarks we can borrow:** `PMC-OA` (PubMed Central), `FUNSD` forms, `DocBank` — general-purpose, not pediatric-Indian. For genuine clinical accuracy numbers, your own fixture set (the 379 PDFs in the bucket, anonymized) is more meaningful than any public benchmark.

**Bottom line:** no pre-built medical module, but the Forge infrastructure is domain-agnostic and perfectly usable for medical. It's already in our testing plan.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Portability Plan — Supabase POC → AWS Production
2	
3	DIS is designed to run on both stacks with identical behavior. This
4	document is the contract that guarantees it.
5	
6	## The two target stacks
7	
8	| Concern         | POC (Supabase)                                                                                                           | Prod (AWS)                                                          |
9	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
10	| Compute         | Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) **or** self-hosted Node.js container on Fly.io/Render if the 150s limit becomes a blocker | ECS Fargate service (Node.js) or Lambda (for short ingest endpoint) |
11	| Object storage  | Supabase Storage                                                                                                         | S3                                                                  |
12	| Database        | Supabase Postgres                                                                                                        | RDS Postgres 16                                                     |
13	| Background jobs | `pg_cron` triggering a `process_pending()` Postgres function that enqueues HTTP calls via `pg_net`                       | SQS + Lambda consumer                                               |
14	| Secrets         | Supabase project secrets                                                                                                 | AWS Secrets Manager                                                 |
15	| Realtime notify | Supabase Realtime (LISTEN/NOTIFY wrapper)                                                                                | AppSync subscriptions / SNS → WebSocket                             |
16	| Auth            | Supabase Auth (JWT)                                                                                                      | Cognito                                                             |
17	| CDN for uploads | Supabase Storage signed URLs                                                                                             | CloudFront + signed URLs                                            |
18	
19	## The three containment boundaries
20	
21	Everything DIS owns falls into one of three layers. Only one of them
22	changes at port time.
23	
24	1. **Pure core (does NOT change at port time).**
25	   `src/core`, `src/ports`, `src/http/routes`, schemas, prompts.
26	2. **Thin wiring (changes once per stack).**
27	   `src/wiring/supabase.ts` vs. `src/wiring/aws.ts`. Select via
28	   `DIS_STACK=supabase|aws`.
29	3. **Adapters (added/removed to match the stack).**
30	   e.g., drop `SupabaseStorageAdapter`, add `S3Adapter`.
31	
32	## Deployment artifact
33	
34	A single `Dockerfile` produces an image that runs anywhere:
35	
36	- Locally (docker-compose).
37	- On Supabase: deployed as an Edge Function **only if runtime allows**;
38	  otherwise deployed to Fly.io/Render and fronted by a Supabase Edge
39	  Function that proxies requests. (Architect's preferred path for POC:
40	  Fly.io free tier for the service itself; Supabase only for DB +
41	  Storage.)
42	- On AWS: same image pushed to ECR and run on Fargate.
43	
44	## Runtime compatibility
45	
46	- **Language:** TypeScript, compiled to Node 20 ESM.
47	- **HTTP framework:** Hono (portable between Node, Deno, Bun, Lambda).
48	- **Postgres client:** `postgres` (no Supabase-specific extensions used
49	  in queries).
50	- **No framework lock-in:** Supabase SDK confined to
51	  `adapters/storage/supabase-storage.ts`,
52	  `adapters/database/supabase-postgres.ts`,
53	  `adapters/secrets/supabase-secrets.ts`,
54	  `adapters/queue/pg-cron.ts`.
55	
56	## Database portability
57	
58	**Rules:**
59	
60	- Migrations are plain SQL (`.sql` files in `dis/migrations/`).
61	- Tool: `node-pg-migrate` or `dbmate`. **Not** `supabase db push` —
62	  that's a Supabase-side convenience only.
63	- No Supabase-specific features in schema: no `supabase_auth.uid()` in
64	  defaults; no `storage.objects` foreign keys.
65	- RLS policies are written with a generic `current_setting('app.user_id')`
66	  pattern; wiring sets this from JWT claims on the respective stack.
67	
68	**Extensions we rely on (both stacks support them):**
69	
70	- `pgcrypto` — UUID generation.
71	- `pg_stat_statements` — metrics.
72	- `pg_trgm` — fuzzy search on test names.
73	
74	Supabase-specific extensions we do **not** use: `pg_graphql`, `pg_net`
75	(only in the pg_cron adapter, which is stack-specific), `supabase_vault`.
76	
77	## Storage portability
78	
79	All storage operations go through `StoragePort`:
80	
81	```ts
82	interface StoragePort {
83	  putObject(input: {
84	    key: string;
85	    body: Buffer;
86	    contentType: string;
87	    metadata?: Record<string, string>;
88	  }): Promise<{ etag: string }>;
89	  getObject(key: string): Promise<{
90	    body: Buffer;
91	    contentType: string;
92	    metadata?: Record<string, string>;
93	  }>;
94	  getSignedUploadUrl(input: {
95	    key: string;
96	    expiresSec: number;
97	    maxSizeBytes: number;
98	    contentType: string;
99	  }): Promise<{ url: string; fields?: Record<string, string> }>;
100	  getSignedDownloadUrl(
101	    key: string,
102	    expiresSec: number,
103	  ): Promise<{ url: string }>;
104	  deleteObject(key: string): Promise<void>;
105	}
106	```
107	
108	Supabase Storage returns public URLs directly; S3 returns pre-signed
109	URLs. Both satisfy the contract.
110	
111	## Queue portability
112	
113	`QueuePort`:
114	
115	```ts
116	interface QueuePort {
117	  enqueue(
118	    topic: string,
119	    payload: Record<string, unknown>,
120	    opts?: { delaySec?: number },
121	  ): Promise<{ messageId: string }>;
122	  startConsumer(
123	    topic: string,
124	    handler: (payload: unknown) => Promise<void>,
125	  ): Promise<void>;
126	}
127	```
128	
129	- POC: `PgCronAdapter` — `enqueue` inserts into `dis_jobs`. A scheduled
130	  `pg_cron` call pulls and dispatches via `pg_net` to the service's
131	  `/internal/process-job` endpoint.
132	- Prod: `SqsAdapter` — enqueue → SQS; consumer → Lambda triggered by SQS.
133	
134	Business logic doesn't know the difference.
135	
136	## Secrets portability
137	
138	`SecretsPort`:
139	
140	```ts
141	interface SecretsPort {
142	  get(name: string): Promise<string>; // throws if not set
143	}
144	```
145	
146	Implementation caches for 5 minutes. Rotation is supported by simply
147	updating the secret at source — adapter picks up on next cache miss.
148	
149	## The porting checklist
150	
151	When moving from Supabase POC to AWS production:
152	
153	1. **Provision AWS resources** (one-time, scripted via Terraform):
154	   RDS, S3 bucket, SQS queue, Secrets Manager entries, ECR repo,
155	   Fargate service, ALB, CloudFront.
156	2. **Migrate database:** `pg_dump` from Supabase; `pg_restore` to RDS.
157	3. **Migrate storage:** `aws s3 cp` with manifest from Supabase Storage.
158	4. **Set env vars on Fargate:** `DIS_STACK=aws`, provider keys from
159	   Secrets Manager, bucket names, queue URLs.
160	5. **Deploy image** from ECR.
161	6. **Smoke test** using the clinical-acceptance fixture set.
162	7. **DNS cutover** with TTL reduced in advance.
163	8. **Leave Supabase running in read-only for 1 week** as a rollback
164	   target.
165	
166	Every step above has a corresponding ticket in `07_tickets/epics.md`
167	under Epic F (Production Port), to be executed only when the product
168	is ready.
169	
170	## Dry-run requirement
171	
172	Before declaring DIS v1 portable, a dry-run is mandated (Epic E ticket):
173	
174	- Spin up AWS account in sandbox.
175	- Run the checklist end-to-end.
176	- Run clinical-acceptance tests against the AWS deployment.
177	- Measure: duration of the port, number of code changes required
178	  (target: zero core changes), manual steps (target: ≤ 3 outside the
179	  script).

84	## Ground rules
85	
86	1. **Core never imports an adapter.** Only ports. Violation = lint error.
87	2. **Adapters never import each other.** They are peers at the edge.
88	3. **Core is pure TypeScript.** No Node-specific APIs. No Supabase SDK.
89	   No AWS SDK. No `fs`, no `fetch`. Core receives dependencies.
90	4. **Adapters are Node-ish but avoid Deno-/Lambda-specific APIs unless
91	   explicitly behind a further shim.** This keeps us runtime-agnostic.
92	5. **All adapters must have a fake for tests.** e.g., `FakeOcrAdapter`
93	   that returns canned results for fixture documents.
94	6. **Adapter swaps are configuration, not deployment.** A `.env`
95	   variable flips provider; the running service picks it up on next
96	   request (5-minute cache max).
97

100	Stored in `ports/*.ts`. The source of truth is the TypeScript file. The
101	TDD shows the canonical shape; adapters must not add undocumented

2	
3	> This is the authoritative architecture document. Every PR references a

7	## §1. Architectural style
8	
9	**Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters)** with a thin event-driven core.
10	
11	- **Core (business logic, pure):** ingestion state machine, confidence
12	  policy evaluator, promotion validator, audit log writer.
13	- **Ports (interfaces):** `OcrPort`, `StructuringPort`, `StoragePort`,
14	  `DatabasePort`, `QueuePort`, `SecretsPort`, `FileRouterPort`,
15	  `PreprocessorPort`.
16	- **Adapters (implementations):** one per port per environment.
17	
18	**Why hexagonal and not layered MVC:** the explicit goal is
19	cloud-and-vendor portability. Ports are the contract; adapters change
20	when the environment changes; core never does.
21	
22	**Secondary pattern:** CQRS-lite — staging (command side,
23	`ocr_extractions`) is separate from production (query side,
24	`lab_results`). Promotion is the explicit command that moves data
25	across the boundary.
26	
27	## §2. High-level components
28	
29	```
30	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
31	│                         DIS CORE                                  │
32	│                                                                   │
33	│   FileRouter → Preprocessor → OcrPort → StructuringPort          │
34	│                                                                   │
35	│   IngestionOrchestrator (state machine)                           │
36	│   ConfidencePolicy                                                │
37	│   PromotionService                                                │
38	│   AuditLogger                                                     │
39	│                                                                   │
40	└───────┬─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────┬──────────┘
41	        │                         │                     │
42	        ▼                         ▼                     ▼
43	┌───────────────┐     ┌────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐
44	│ StoragePort   │     │ DatabasePort       │  │ QueuePort      │
45	│               │     │                    │  │                │
46	│ Supabase → S3 │     │ Supabase → RDS     │  │ pg_cron → SQS  │
47	└───────────────┘     └────────────────────┘  └────────────────┘
48	```

50	## §3. Service boundary
51	
52	- **Transport:** HTTPS, JSON.
53	- **Exposed API:** OpenAPI 3.1 spec in `04_api/openapi.yaml`.
54	- **Authentication:** bearer token (Supabase anon key on POC, Cognito JWT on prod). Never the service role key from the browser.
55	- **Authorization:** database RLS + service-role key on internal promotion paths.
56	
57	The only browser-facing entry points are:
58	
59	| Path                                     | Purpose                                                     |
60	| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
61	| `POST /ingest`                           | Submit a new document. Returns `extraction_id` immediately. |
62	| `GET /extractions/:id`                   | Read extraction status + data for the verification UI.      |
63	| `POST /extractions/:id/approve`          | Nurse approves (optionally with edits).                     |
64	| `POST /extractions/:id/reject`           | Nurse rejects with reason code.                             |
65	| `GET /extractions?status=pending_review` | Queue page.                                                 |
66	| `GET /admin/metrics`                     | Admin dashboard. Service-role only.                         |
67	
68	Realtime status changes push through Supabase Realtime / (AWS: AppSync
69	subscriptions). Fallback: 5 s polling.
70	
71	## §4. State machine
72	
73	```
74	  uploaded
75	     │
76	     ├── (FileRouter: native PDF / DOCX / XLSX)
77	     │   ▼
78	     │  structuring
79	     │     │
80	     │     ▼
81	     │   ready_for_review  ──► verified  ──► promoted
82	     │     │                      │
83	     │     │                      └► (nurse rejects) rejected
84	     │     │
85	     │     └─(fail)──► failed
86	     │
87	     └── (FileRouter: scan / image)
88	          ▼
89	         preprocessing
90	          │
91	          ▼
92	         ocr
93	          │
94	          ▼
95	         structuring  ──► (as above)
96	```
97	
98	All transitions are recorded in `ocr_audit_log`. Only valid transitions
99	are permitted in code — attempts to violate the state machine raise a
100	domain exception.
101	
102	## §5. Idempotency
103	
104	- **Ingest:** `POST /ingest` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header
105	  (client generates UUIDv4). The server stores the key in
106	  `ocr_extractions.idempotency_key UNIQUE`. Duplicate submission returns
107	  the existing row.
108	- **Approve/Reject:** same mechanism on state-changing endpoints to
109	  avoid double-promotion from network retries.
110	- **Promotion:** CS-11 duplicate-row check (patient + test + date + value).
111	
112	## §6. Concurrency & locking
113	
114	- Extraction rows carry a `version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` column.
115	- Approve/reject sends the version; server uses optimistic lock
116	  (`UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`).
117	- On conflict, return 409 with the current state; client reloads.
118	
119	## §7. File routing decision tree
120	
121	```
122	ext in (pdf)
123	 └ try pdf.js text extraction
124	    └ text length ≥ threshold (≥100 chars/page average)?
125	       ├ yes → path: NATIVE_TEXT
126	       └ no  → path: OCR_SCAN
127	ext in (jpg, jpeg, png, heic, webp, bmp, tiff)
128	 └ path: OCR_IMAGE
129	ext in (docx, doc)
130	 └ path: OFFICE_WORD
131	ext in (xlsx, xls, csv)
132	 └ path: OFFICE_SHEET
133	anything else
134	 └ reject (415 Unsupported Media Type)
135	```
136	
137	Threshold is configurable via `DIS_NATIVE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE` (default 100).
138	
139	## §8. Preprocessing pipeline (OCR paths only)
140	
141	In order:
142	
143	1. **Normalize container** — HEIC/WebP/BMP/TIFF → JPEG; multi-page TIFF → JPEG per frame.
144	2. **Deskew** — detect tilt via Hough lines; rotate to ≤ ±1°.
145	3. **Perspective correction** — corner detection; warp to rectangle.
146	4. **Blank-page detection** — drop pages with <0.5% ink density.
147	5. **Duplicate-page detection** — perceptual hash; drop near-duplicates.
148	6. **Resize** — max 1920 px longest side.
149	7. **Contrast enhancement** — adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE).
150	8. **JPEG encode** — quality 85.
151	9. **Page count cap** — refuse if >50 pages (config: `DIS_MAX_PAGES`).
152	
153	Emits `PreprocessedDocument { pages: Buffer[], dropped: {blank, duplicate}, original_page_count }`.
154

1	# Glossary
2	
3	Terminology used consistently across all DIS documentation. Agents MUST
4	use these exact terms in code, tests, commits, and docs. No synonyms.
5	
6	| Term                    | Definition                                                                                      |
7	| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
8	| **DIS**                 | Document Ingestion Service — the subject of this plan.                                          |
9	| **Ingestion**           | The complete lifecycle: upload → parse/OCR → structure → verify → promote.                      |
10	| **Extraction**          | A single row in `ocr_extractions` representing one document's full lifecycle state.             |
11	| **Extraction ID**       | UUID primary key of `ocr_extractions`. The canonical reference to an ingestion.                 |
12	| **Raw response**        | The unmodified JSON returned by the OCR provider (Datalab `/convert`).                          |
13	| **Structured data**     | The clinical JSON produced by the Structuring Adapter from the raw response.                    |
14	| **Block**               | A typed region of a document as emitted by Chandra: `{block_type, bbox, content, confidence?}`. |
15	| **Staging**             | The pre-verified state. Data exists in `ocr_extractions` only, not yet in clinical tables.      |
16	| **Promotion**           | The act of copying verified fields from `ocr_extractions` into `lab_results` / `vaccinations`.  |
17	| **Verification**        | Human review step: approve, edit-then-approve, or reject.                                       |
18	| **Auto-approval**       | Machine-executed promotion without human review when confidence thresholds are met.             |
19	| **Clinical tables**     | `lab_results`, `vaccinations`, and `visits.attached_documents` — anything a doctor consumes.    |
20	| **File Router**         | Component that decides native-text extraction vs. OCR vs. office-parser.                        |
21	| **Preprocessor**        | Component that deskews, compresses, drops blank pages before OCR.                               |
22	| **OCR Adapter**         | Pluggable provider of `OcrResult` (Datalab, on-prem Chandra, Claude Vision).                    |
23	| **Structuring Adapter** | Pluggable LLM that turns Markdown/blocks into clinical JSON (Claude Haiku default).             |
24	| **Port / Adapter**      | Hexagonal-architecture terms. **Port** = interface; **Adapter** = implementation.               |
25	| **Shadow mode**         | New pipeline runs in parallel with old one; output compared, not shown to users.                |
26	| **Kill switch**         | Feature flag that routes all traffic back to the legacy `process-document`.                     |
27	| **POC stack**           | Supabase (Edge Functions + Postgres + Storage).                                                 |
28	| **Prod stack**          | AWS (ECS/Lambda + RDS Postgres + S3).                                                           |
29	| **Native PDF**          | A PDF whose text is embedded as selectable characters (no OCR needed).                          |
30	| **Scan PDF**            | A PDF that is a wrapper around raster images — requires OCR.                                    |
31	| **Confidence gate**     | Policy that maps `(block_type, confidence_score) → auto_approve                                 | needs_review`. |
32	| **Ticket**              | A single unit of work tracked under `07_tickets/`.                                              |
33	| **DoD**                 | Definition of Done — the checklist every ticket must satisfy before merge.                      |
34	| **Clinical reviewer**   | The human clinician listed in `08_team/RACI.md` who reviews safety-tagged tickets.              |

1	# Product Brief
2	
3	## Problem
4	
5	Reception and nurses upload medical documents (lab reports, discharge
6	summaries, prescriptions, vaccination cards) during patient registration.
7	The current pipeline extracts clinical fields using Claude Sonnet 4 Vision
8	and writes them directly into `lab_results`, `vaccinations`, and
9	`visits.attached_documents`. No human verifies the extraction. There is
10	no audit trail of the raw model output. Re-processing creates duplicate
11	rows. The model provider and cloud provider are both baked into the
12	Edge Function.
13	
14	## Proposal
15	
16	Replace the single-step pipeline with a staged, verification-gated
17	Document Ingestion Service. All OCR-derived data lands first in a
18	staging table. A nurse reviews, optionally edits, and approves. Only
19	approved data reaches clinical tables. The raw model output is
20	preserved indefinitely for audit and reproducibility.
21	
22	Architecturally, separate the service into Ports & Adapters so the OCR
23	provider, the structuring LLM, the storage backend, and the database
24	can each be swapped without touching business logic.
25	
26	## Users
27	
28	| Role             | Interaction with DIS                                                                                                             |
29	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
30	| Reception clerk  | Uploads files at registration. Unchanged UX. Sees a "Processing" → "Ready for review" status instead of "AI extracted: …" today. |
31	| Nurse / verifier | **New role in this flow.** Opens the Verification UI, reviews extracted fields side-by-side with the source, approves or edits.  |
32	| Doctor           | Reads verified labs on the prescription pad. Never sees unverified OCR output again.                                             |
33	| System admin     | Monitors extraction queue, handles stuck jobs, rotates provider keys.                                                            |
34	
35	## Success criteria
36	
37	Measured 30 days after default rollout:
38	
39	1. **Zero unverified clinical rows.** Every row in `lab_results` created
40	   by DIS has a non-null `ocr_extraction_id` or `verified_by` (manual).
41	2. **>95% of extractions verified within 4 hours** during business hours.
42	3. **Nurse edit rate <30%** — most extractions approved as-is. If
43	   higher, it's a signal to improve prompts or preprocessing.
44	4. **Per-document cost <= current cost.** Target: at least 30% cheaper
45	   via Chandra + Haiku vs. Sonnet Vision.
46	5. **P95 end-to-end latency (upload → ready-for-review) <= 60 s.**
47	6. **Zero clinical-safety incidents** attributable to an un-audited OCR row.
48	7. **The service can be redeployed to a fresh AWS account in one working
49	   day** using only the portability plan — proven via a dry-run.
50	
51	## Scope (v1)
52	
53	**In scope:**
54	
55	- New `ocr_extractions` table + FK column on `lab_results` and `vaccinations`.
56	- New HTTP service with file router, preprocessor, OCR adapter, structuring adapter.
57	- Datalab `/convert` integration.
58	- Claude Haiku integration for structuring.
59	- Confidence-gated auto-approval policy (off by default; opt-in per deployment).
60	- Verification UI (new page).
61	- Rollout via feature flag: shadow → opt-in → default.
62	- Portability adapters: `StorageAdapter`, `DatabaseAdapter`, `SecretsAdapter`, `QueueAdapter`.
63	- Comprehensive test suite including clinical acceptance tests.
64	- Runbooks for incident response.
65	
66	**Explicitly out of scope** — see `00_overview/non_goals.md`.
67	
68	## Assumptions
69	
70	- Datalab hosted API remains available with current pricing.
71	- Claude Haiku produces JSON reliably when given a strong schema prompt.
72	- Nurses have a ~5-minute window during/after registration for verification.
73	- Clinical team accepts the latency tradeoff (verification adds human time, but removes clinical risk).
74	- Daily document volume stays under 100/day during POC — relevant for Supabase free-tier sizing.
75	
76	## Risks and mitigations
77	
78	| Risk                                           | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                                                                             |
79	| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
80	| Datalab API outage                             | M          | H      | Fallback adapter → Claude Vision. Kill switch → legacy `process-document`.                             |
81	| Claude Haiku JSON drift                        | M          | M      | Schema validation on every response; on failure, re-prompt with `strict: true` or fall back to Sonnet. |
82	| Verification backlog grows                     | M          | H      | Alerting at queue depth > 20; nurse role is accountable per RACI.                                      |
83	| Nurse fatigue → rubber-stamp approvals         | H          | H      | UI shows diff-from-Claude if edited; weekly sample audit by clinician.                                 |
84	| Migration collision with live data             | L          | H      | All new columns are nullable; deploys via shadow mode first.                                           |
85	| Supabase free-tier storage cap                 | H          | M      | PDF compression on ingest; planned S3 migration at 70% capacity.                                       |
86	| Claude/Datalab key leak                        | L          | H      | Keys in secrets manager only; rotation runbook; CI secret-scan.                                        |
87	| Model hallucination slips through verification | M          | H      | Clinical reviewer does weekly sample audit. Metrics track override rate.                               |
88	
89	## Out-of-the-box wins
90	
91	- Raw audit trail → satisfies NABH documentation expectations far better than current.
92	- Adapter layer → buys future optionality (on-prem Chandra, GPT, Gemini) with no rewrites.
93	- Decoupled structuring LLM → cost tuning dial (Haiku now, Sonnet for hard cases, local model later).
94	- Verification UI → gives nurses ownership, reduces doctor cognitive load.

the old one is kept for audit. 48 - A "Retry" action is logged with operator ID and timestamp. 49 50 --- 51 52 ## Nurse / verifier 53 54 ### DIS-US-010 — See the verification queue 55 56 As a nurse, 57 I want to see a list of extractions awaiting my review, 58 so that I know what to work on and in what order. 59 60 **Acceptance criteria:** 61 62 - Queue page lists all `pending_review` extractions, oldest first. 63 - Each row shows: patient name + UHID, document category, uploaded time, 64 confidence badge (green/yellow/red), and thumbnail. 65 - Queue auto-refreshes every 30 s. 66 - Filter by category, by uploader, by age. 67 68 ### DIS-US-011 — Verify an extraction side-by-side 69 70 As a nurse, 71 I want to see the original document and the extracted fields side-by-side, 72 so that I can compare quickly. 73 74 **Acceptance criteria:** 75 76 - Left pane: source document viewer (PDF.js for PDFs, `` for images). 77 - Right pane: editable form with all extracted fields grouped by entity 78 (labs, vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, summary). 79 - Each field shows its confidence; low-confidence fields are highlighted. 80 - Bounding-box overlay on the source when a field is hovered (when 81 `bbox` is present in the raw response). 82 83 ### DIS-US-012 — Approve an extraction 84 85 As a nurse, 86 I want a single action to approve a clean extraction, 87 so that verification is fast when the AI is right. 88 89 **Acceptance criteria:** 90 91 - "Approve all" button disabled until all required fields pass validation. 92 - On approve, rows are written to `lab_results` / `vaccinations`, 93 `ocr_extractions.status` flips to `verified`, `verified_by` and 94 `verified_at` are set. 95 - Success toast shows exactly how many rows were written. 96 - An audit row is inserted in `ocr_audit_log`. 97 98 ### DIS-US-013 — Edit a value before approving 99 100 As a nurse, 101 I want to correct an extracted value before approving, 102 so that the clinical table receives the correct data. 103 104 **Acceptance criteria:** 105 106 - Every field is editable. 107 - Original AI value is preserved in the extraction row (JSON column `raw_structured`). 108 - The verified value is stored separately (`verified_structured`). 109 - The audit log records the before/after per edited field. 110 111 ### DIS-US-014 — Reject an extraction 112 113 As a nurse, 114 I want to reject an extraction that is junk, 115 so that no bad data leaks into clinical tables. 116 117 **Acceptance criteria:** 118 119 - Reject requires a reason code (dropdown: `illegible`, `wrong_patient`, 120 `not_medical`, `duplicate`, `other`). 121 - If "other", a free-text note is required. 122 - Rejected extractions never promote. They remain in `ocr_extractions` 123 with status `rejected`. 124 125 ### DIS-US-015 — Handle a duplicate document 126 127 As a nurse, 128 I want the system to warn me if an identical document was already 129 verified, 130 so that I don't create duplicate lab rows. 131 132 **Acceptance criteria:** 133 134 - On open, the verification UI checks for extractions with the same 135 `content_hash` already in `verified` state. 136 - If found, a banner shows the prior verified extraction ID and a 137 "This looks like a duplicate" warning. 138 - Nurse can still approve (explicit override, logged). 139 140 --- 141 142 ## Doctor 143 144 ### DIS-US-020 — Doctor sees only verified labs 145 146 As a doctor, 147 I want the prescription pad to show only verified lab values, 148 so that I don't make decisions on un-checked OCR output. 149 150 **Acceptance criteria:** 151 152 - `get_lab_history` tool in `generate-prescription` applies the same filter. 156 157 ### DIS-US-021 — Doctor can see which labs are AI-originated 158 159 As a doctor, 160 I want a visual indicator on labs that came from AI extraction, 161 so that I can apply appropriate judgment. 162 163 **Acceptance criteria:** 164 165 - A small `AI` badge renders beside any lab row where `source = 'ai_extracted'` 166 and `verification_status = 'verified'`. 167 - Hover shows verifier name + time. 168 169 --- 170 171 ## System admin 172 173 ### DIS-US-030 — Monitor the queue 174 175 As an admin, 176 I want to see queue depth and processing latency, 177 so that I can intervene when the system is overloaded. 178 179 **Acceptance criteria:** 180 181 - `DIS_KILL_SWITCH=1` env var (read on every request) redirects the 209 public endpoint to the legacy Edge Function behavior. 210 - Kill switch change is logged. 211 - Documented in runbook.

3	All DIS tables live in the same Postgres database as the rest of the
4	application. Tables are prefixed `dis_` OR use verbose clinical names
5	(`ocr_extractions`, `ocr_audit_log`) for those that reference clinical
6	concepts directly.

68	```sql

70	  id               bigserial primary key,
71	  extraction_id    uuid not null references ocr_extractions(id) on delete restrict,

6	## Order of migrations (non-breaking by design)
7	
8	All migrations are **additive and reversible** until the cutover
9	migration (M-008), which is applied only after feature-flag default
10	rollout.
11	
12	### M-001: Create `ocr_extractions`
13	
14	Adds the staging table and indexes. No clinical impact.
15	
16	### M-002: Create `ocr_audit_log` with append-only triggers
17	
18	Adds audit log. Safe.
19	
20	### M-003: Create `dis_confidence_policy`
21	
22	Adds policy table + seeds row with `enabled=false`.
23	
24	### M-004: Create `dis_jobs` (POC only — AWS uses SQS)
25	
26	Env-gated: only runs when `DIS_STACK=supabase`.
27	
28	### M-005: Create `dis_cost_ledger`
29	
30	Append-only cost tracking.
31	
32	### M-006: Add nullable columns to `lab_results` and `vaccinations`
33	
34	- `ocr_extraction_id` nullable FK
35	- `verification_status` NOT NULL with DEFAULT (existing rows get default)
36	- `verified_by`, `verified_at` nullable
37	
38	Backfill step inside the migration sets `verification_status` based on
39	the legacy `source` column.
40	
41	### M-007: Add unique dedupe indexes
42	
43	`uniq_lab_dedupe`, `uniq_vax_dedupe`. Migration includes a dry-run
44	check: if any duplicates exist, migration aborts and prints a list for
45	manual resolution.
46	
47	### M-008: RLS policies on `ocr_extractions` and related
48	
49	Non-breaking — pre-existing tables retain their policies.
50	
51	### M-009 (cutover, applied post-rollout): make FK mandatory on new rows
52	
53	```sql
54	alter table lab_results add constraint lab_results_extraction_or_source
55	  check (
56	    ocr_extraction_id is not null
57	    or verification_status in ('manual','verified') -- manual entry is still allowed
58	  );
59	```
60	
61	## Reversibility
62	
63	Each migration has a `.rollback.sql`:
64	
65	- M-001 to M-005: `DROP TABLE … CASCADE`.
66	- M-006: `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN …`.
67	- M-007: `DROP INDEX …`.
68	- M-008: `DROP POLICY …`.
69	- M-009: `DROP CONSTRAINT …`.
70	
71	Rollback scripts are tested in CI — a migration cannot merge if its
72	rollback doesn't restore the schema to the previous state byte-for-byte
73	(checked via `pg_dump --schema-only` diff).

content.text:
**Rough monthly cost for POC volume:**

**Assumptions** (from our conversation): ~20 documents/day × 30 days = 600 docs/month. Average 2 pages/doc (most are 1-page OPD slips; discharge summaries are longer). Using Datalab's **accurate mode** (Chandra) = $4.50 per 1,000 pages.

**Calculation:**
- 600 docs × 2 pages = 1,200 pages/month
- Pages cost: 1,200 × $4.50 / 1,000 = **$5.40**
- Plan fee: **$25/month** (includes $25 credit)
- $25 credit covers the $5.40 usage ~4× over → **effective monthly cost: $25 flat**

**Minimum-charge trap to watch:** $0.01/request means every API call costs at least 1 cent even for tiny docs. At 600 docs × $0.01 = $6/month floor — still well under the $25 credit.

**When you'd exceed $25:** if usage crosses ~5,500 pages/month (≈ 2,750 docs at 2 pages each). You'd start paying overage at $4.50/1,000 pages beyond that.

**Plus Claude Haiku** for structuring: ~$0.002/doc × 600 = **$1.20/month** (negligible).

**Total POC monthly budget: ~$26.20** — basically the $25 flat plus a dollar of Anthropic usage. Comfortable headroom for 4× the current volume before overages kick in.

**Yes — here's the scaling curve.**

| Daily docs | Pages/month (2pp avg) | Datalab cost | Haiku cost | **Total/month** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 (current POC) | 1,200 | $25 (flat) | $1 | **$26** |
| 50 | 3,000 | $25 (still within credit) | $3 | **$28** |
| 100 | 6,000 | $25 + (500 × $4.50/1k) = $27.25 | $6 | **$33** |
| 250 | 15,000 | $25 + $45 = $70 | $15 | **$85** |
| 500 | 30,000 | $25 + $112.50 = $137.50 | $30 | **$168** |
| 1,000 | 60,000 | $25 + $247.50 = $272.50 | $60 | **$333** |
| 2,500 | 150,000 | $25 + $652.50 = $677.50 | $150 | **$828** |

**Key inflection points:**

- **Up to ~90 docs/day** → you stay inside the $25 credit. Effective cost is flat.
- **At ~500 docs/day** → ~$170/month. Still cheaper than Claude Vision would be at the same volume (~$600-900/month).
- **At ~1,000+ docs/day** → self-hosting Chandra on a GPU (~$200-400/month fixed) starts to break even vs. hosted API.

**Per-document cost stabilizes at ≈ ₹28 per document (~$0.33) at high volume** — vs. Claude Vision today at ₹70-170 per document.

**Practical rule of thumb:** stay on hosted until you cross ~1,000 docs/day consistently for 2+ months. Then reassess on-prem.

**Yes — 1,000 docs/day is your switch-point to self-hosted Chandra.** Worth remembering, with three caveats:

**The caveats:**

1. **Sustained, not peak.** A single busy day at 1,200 docs doesn't justify buying a GPU. Trigger is 1,000+/day averaged over 60 days.
2. **Hosted cost at that point: ~$330/month. Self-hosted floor: ~$200-400/month** (GPU 24/7) + engineering time to run it. The gap is small — the real switch reason beyond ~1,000 docs/day is usually **data residency** (ABDM/PHI on-prem) or **latency control**, not cost savings alone.
3. **Hybrid is an option.** You can keep hosted for normal flow and spin up on-prem Chandra only for sensitive docs or batch backlogs — the adapter pattern in our TDD supports this by design.

Let me save this to memory so it persists across sessions.

---
name: Chandra hosted-to-on-prem inflection point
description: The document-volume threshold at which moving from Datalab's hosted Chandra API to self-hosted Chandra becomes worth evaluating for this project.
type: project
---

**Fact:** 1,000 documents/day (sustained, 60-day average) is the switch-point where self-hosted Chandra becomes worth evaluating vs. Datalab's hosted API.

**Why:** At 1,000 docs/day (~60,000 pages/month), Datalab hosted costs ~$333/month (OCR + Haiku structuring). A GPU instance (AWS g5.xlarge / GCP L4, 24/7) costs ~$200-400/month. The dollar gap is small — the real trigger beyond cost is typically **data residency (ABDM / PHI on-prem)** or **latency control**, not pure savings.

**How to apply:**
- Below 1,000 docs/day: stay on Datalab hosted (`DIS_OCR_PROVIDER=datalab`).
- At sustained 1,000+ docs/day for 2+ months: evaluate on-prem; spin up the `OnpremChandraAdapter` (stubbed in DIS v1).
- Hybrid is valid: hosted for normal flow + on-prem for sensitive docs or batch backlogs — the DIS adapter pattern supports this by design.
- Do NOT switch on a single busy day or a peak; sustained average only.

**Pricing anchor points (as of 2026-04-20):**
- Datalab Cloud-Hosted plan: $25/month flat, includes $25 credit, then $4.50/1,000 pages accurate-mode (Chandra), $3.00/1,000 pages markdown/layout, min $0.01/request.
- Claude Haiku structuring: ~$2/1,000 docs.
- POC current volume (~20 docs/day): ~$26/month total — flat plan covers everything.

# Team & RACI

> DIS is executed agentically. Humans hold veto authority on safety-tagged
> tickets and on the integration gate. The matrix below makes that
> explicit.

## Roles

| Role | Filled by | Primary responsibility |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| **Product Owner (PO)** | Dr. Lokender Goyal (user) | Scope, prioritization, clinical sign-off on phases |
| **Architect / Tech Lead / QA Lead** | Claude (orchestrator) | Owns TDD, ticket backlog, review gates, DoD enforcement |
| **Clinical Reviewer** | Dr. Lokender Goyal (and any designated co-clinician) | Second human review on every `clinical-safety` ticket; weekly sample audit |
| **Backend Agent(s)** | `general-purpose` or `feature-dev:code-architect` | Implement tickets in `dis/src/core/`, `dis/src/adapters/`, migrations |
| **Frontend Agent** | `general-purpose` + `frontend-design:frontend-design` | Verification UI (new page, not registration/pad) |
| **QA Agent** | `general-purpose` | Write unit + integration + clinical-acceptance tests first (TDD) |
| **SRE / Ops Agent** | `general-purpose` | Runbooks, CI, monitoring, deploy automation |
| **Port Validator** | `agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts` or equivalent lint agent | Enforce "core imports no adapter" rule on every PR |
| **Security Reviewer** | `/security-review` skill agent + human on demand | Key handling, RLS policies, CI secret scans |
| **Integration Gatekeeper** | Dr. Lokender Goyal (user) | **Sole** authority to approve any ticket that modifies `web/`, existing Edge Functions, or live schema |

## RACI matrix

**R** = Responsible (does the work) · **A** = Accountable (owns outcome) · **C** = Consulted · **I** = Informed

| Activity | PO | Architect | Clinical Rev. | Backend | Frontend | QA | SRE | Security | Integration Gate |
|----------|----|-----------|--------------|---------|----------|----|----|----------|-------------------|
| Set scope & priorities | **A** | R | C | I | I | I | I | I | — |
| Write / change TDD | C | **A**/R | C | C | C | C | C | C | — |
| Implement a core/adapter ticket | I | A | — | **R** | — | C | — | — | — |
| Implement verification UI ticket | I | A | C | — | **R** | C | — | — | — |
| Write tests for a ticket | I | A | — | C | C | **R** | — | — | — |
| Review clinical-safety ticket | C | A | **R** (veto) | C | C | C | — | — | — |
| Approve integration with existing system | **R**/A | C | C | — | — | — | — | — | **R** (gate) |
| Migration dry-run / apply | I | A | — | R | — | R | **R** | — | — |
| Key rotation | I | A | — | — | — | — | **R** | C | — |
| Security review | I | A | — | C | C | C | C | **R** | — |
| Rollout phase advance | **R**/A | R | C (veto on safety) | I | I | C | C | I | I |
| Incident response | I | A | C (if clinical) | R | R | R | **R** | C | — |
| Weekly clinical audit | A | I | **R** | — | — | — | — | — | — |

## Review gates (binding on every ticket)

See `08_team/review_gates.md` for the full checklist. Summary:

1. **Pre-start:** ticket has acceptance criteria, dependencies resolved, TDD reference.
2. **Test-first:** a failing test is committed before implementation starts.
3. **Code review:** another agent OR a human reviews the PR.
4. **Clinical-safety gate** (tickets tagged `clinical-safety`): human clinician signs off. **No exceptions.**
5. **Integration gate** (tickets tagged `integration`): user's explicit written approval required in the PR thread. **No exceptions.**
6. **Port validator:** automated check — core must not import any adapter.
7. **CI gate:** tests pass, migrations round-trip, no secrets in diff.
8. **DoD:** acceptance criteria checked, docs updated, changelog entry added.

## Ticket tags that alter the review path

| Tag | Effect |
|-----|--------|
| `clinical-safety` | Requires Clinical Reviewer sign-off (RACI row R). Maps to one of CS-1..CS-12. |
| `integration` | Requires Integration Gatekeeper (user) sign-off. Cannot be auto-merged. |
| `migration` | Requires SRE + Architect joint review; includes CI round-trip test. |
| `security` | Requires Security Reviewer sign-off. |
| `breaking` | Requires ADR + Architect sign-off. |
| `doc-only` | No test requirement; still goes through code review. |

## Escalation

- **Blocked ticket > 24 h:** agent opens a clarification in `07_tickets/clarifications/`; Architect responds within 4 h business hours.
- **Clinical-safety concern raised mid-ticket:** stop immediately, escalate to Clinical Reviewer before any further commit.
- **Suspected data leak / key exposure:** trigger `09_runbooks/incident_response.md` SEV1 path; page Security Reviewer.

## Out-of-band duties

- **Weekly clinical audit:** Clinical Reviewer samples 10 verified extractions each Monday and compares to source. Results logged in `dis/audits/YYYY-WW.md`. Two consecutive weeks with >10% error rate triggers an investigation ticket.
- **Monthly cost review:** PO + Architect review `dis_cost_ledger`. If cost/doc exceeds target by 25%, open an optimization ticket.
- **Quarterly DR drill:** SRE executes `09_runbooks/dr_and_backup.md` restore procedure. Drill outcome logged.

## Hand-offs with the existing team

- **Reception clerk:** trained on new "Processing / Ready for review" status badge during opt-in phase. Training material in `06_rollout/comms_and_training.md`.
- **Nurse / verifier:** trained on the verification UI before opt-in. Dedicated onboarding session (recorded).
- **Doctor:** informed of the `AI` badge on lab rows. No training required; the badge is a passive indicator.
- **Admin / IT:** runbooks live in `09_runbooks/`; on-call rotation defined when we have > 1 admin.

# Review Gates

Every ticket passes through this exact sequence of gates. No gate may
be skipped, waived, or combined. Agents that bypass a gate have their
PR rejected automatically.

## The gate sequence

```
[1] Pre-start gate
  └── [2] Test-first gate
        └── [3] Implementation
              └── [4] Automated checks gate
                    └── [5] Code review gate
                          └── [6] Safety / integration / security gate (conditional)
                                └── [7] DoD gate
                                      └── Merge
```

Each gate has an explicit pass criterion, an owner, and an action on
failure.

---

## Gate 1 — Pre-start

**Purpose:** ensure the ticket is executable before an agent begins.

**Owner:** Architect (reviews on ticket creation)

**Pass criteria:**
- Ticket has a unique `DIS-###` ID.
- Ticket references the TDD section(s) it implements (e.g. `implements TDD §9.2`).
- Acceptance criteria are numbered and testable.
- Dependencies (if any) are listed by ticket ID AND are in `Done` status.
- "Out of scope" list is explicit.
- Tags applied (at least one of: `core`, `adapter`, `ui`, `migration`, `test`, `doc-only`; plus any special tag from `08_team/RACI.md`).

**Fail action:** ticket status flips to `Blocked — needs clarification`; Architect either updates the ticket or creates a clarification ticket.

---

## Gate 2 — Test-first

**Purpose:** enforce TDD. No implementation without a failing test.

**Owner:** QA Agent (proposes test); Architect (approves)

**Pass criteria:**
- A test file exists at the expected path (per `05_testing/`).
- The test contains at least one assertion tied to an acceptance criterion.
- Running the test locally **fails** with a predictable error (e.g. "not implemented", "undefined export").
- The failing test is committed on the ticket's branch before any implementation commit.

**Fail action:** implementation ticket status stays `Not Started`. Developer agent may not begin.

**Exception:** tickets tagged `doc-only` skip this gate. No implementation code, no tests required — but the doc change itself is reviewed via Gate 5.

---

## Gate 3 — Implementation

**Purpose:** actual work. Not a gate per se, but tracked for visibility.

**Rules during implementation:**
- Scope is frozen to the acceptance criteria. Any scope change requires a new ticket.
- No modifications to files outside the ticket's declared file list.
- Commit messages follow `[DIS-###] <summary> — implements TDD §X.Y` format.
- Tests from Gate 2 turn green incrementally; they do not get deleted or weakened.

---

## Gate 4 — Automated checks

**Purpose:** the machine-checkable must pass before humans look.

**Owner:** CI

**Pass criteria (all must be green):**
- Lint (ESLint + Prettier — no changes in format-check).
- Type-check (`tsc --noEmit`).
- Unit tests pass (100% of suite, not just this ticket's).
- Integration tests pass against sandbox adapters.
- Port validator passes: no `import` from `adapters/` inside `core/` or `ports/`.
- Schema round-trip test (if `migration` tag): up-down-up produces identical schema dump.
- Secret-scan clean (no keys in diff).
- OpenAPI schema is valid and unchanged (or changes are in a dedicated `api-change` ticket).

**Fail action:** PR marked draft; agent fixes and re-runs. No human review until green.

---

## Gate 5 — Code review

**Purpose:** an independent pair of eyes.

**Owner:** A second agent OR a human. Clinical-safety tickets require a human; see Gate 6.

**Pass criteria:**
- At least one `Approved` review by a non-author.
- All review comments addressed (either fixed or explicitly deferred to a follow-up ticket).
- Reviewer has verified: acceptance criteria met, tests cover the changes, documentation updated.

**Fail action:** PR remains open with `Changes Requested`. Author iterates.

---

## Gate 6 — Conditional gates (any that apply)

### 6a. Clinical-safety gate

**Triggered by:** tag `clinical-safety`. Applies to any ticket implementing CS-1..CS-12 or touching extraction-to-clinical promotion.

**Owner:** Clinical Reviewer (human clinician from `RACI.md`)

**Pass criteria:**
- Clinical Reviewer has written `CLINICAL APPROVED — <name>, <date>` in the PR thread.
- If edits were made after clinical review, re-approval is required.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge. No override.

### 6b. Integration gate

**Triggered by:** tag `integration`. Applies to any ticket that:
- Modifies files under `web/`, or
- Modifies existing Edge Functions in `supabase/functions/` (including `process-document`), or
- Applies DIS migrations to the live Supabase database, or
- Adds any reference to DIS from existing registration / prescription-pad / generate-prescription flows.

**Owner:** Integration Gatekeeper (user — Dr. Lokender Goyal)

**Pass criteria:**
- Integration Gatekeeper has written `INTEGRATION APPROVED — <name>, <date>` in the PR thread.
- The approval explicitly states what is being integrated.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge. No override. No integration ticket is auto-executable.

### 6c. Security gate

**Triggered by:** tag `security`. Applies to auth changes, secret handling, RLS policy changes, any network-boundary changes.

**Owner:** Security Reviewer

**Pass criteria:**
- Security Reviewer has run `/security-review` and resolved any HIGH/CRITICAL findings.
- CI secret-scan is clean.
- No credentials in logs, error messages, or commit history.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge.

### 6d. Breaking-change gate

**Triggered by:** tag `breaking`. Applies to port interface changes, schema breaks, API contract breaks.

**Owner:** Architect

**Pass criteria:**
- An ADR exists in `02_architecture/adrs/NNNN-title.md`.
- All consumers are updated in the same PR OR are on a named follow-up ticket list.
- Architect has written `BREAKING APPROVED` in the PR thread.

---

## Gate 7 — Definition of Done

**Purpose:** final pre-merge checklist.

**Owner:** Author (self-check) + final reviewer (cross-check)

**Checklist:**
- [ ] All acceptance criteria checked off with evidence linked (test names, screenshots, log excerpts).
- [ ] TDD updated if architecture changed.
- [ ] OpenAPI updated if API changed.
- [ ] Runbook updated if operational surface changed.
- [ ] `ROADMAP.md` / ticket board updated with `Done`.
- [ ] No TODO / FIXME / `console.log` in production code paths.
- [ ] Changelog entry added (`dis/CHANGELOG.md`).
- [ ] Audit log entry added for migration tickets.

**Fail action:** PR reopened; author addresses gaps.

---

## Merge mechanics

- Merge method: **squash-and-merge** for feature tickets; **rebase-and-merge** for migrations (so each migration is one commit). No regular merges except between agent branches and `feat/dis-plan`/development branches (per `windows-parallel-agents` orchestrator flow).
- The Architect is the only role that can merge to the main integration branch.
- Branch naming: `feat/dis-<agent-id>` for agent work; `feat/dis-###-<slug>` for implementation tickets.

## Emergency override

There is **no emergency override** for Gates 6a (clinical-safety) or 6b
(integration). If the situation is truly urgent, escalate to SEV1 and
follow `09_runbooks/incident_response.md` — that path has its own
authority model and explicit post-hoc review requirement.

**Exception:** tickets tagged `doc-only` skip this gate. No implementation code, no tests required — but the doc change itself is reviewed via Gate 5.

---

## Gate 3 — Implementation

**Purpose:** actual work. Not a gate per se, but tracked for visibility.

**Rules during implementation:**
- Scope is frozen to the acceptance criteria. Any scope change requires a new ticket.
- No modifications to files outside the ticket's declared file list.
- Commit messages follow `[DIS-###] <summary> — implements TDD §X.Y` format.
- Tests from Gate 2 turn green incrementally; they do not get deleted or weakened.

---

## Gate 4 — Automated checks

**Purpose:** the machine-checkable must pass before humans look.

**Owner:** CI

**Pass criteria (all must be green):**
- Lint (ESLint + Prettier — no changes in format-check).
- Type-check (`tsc --noEmit`).
- Unit tests pass (100% of suite, not just this ticket's).
- Integration tests pass against sandbox adapters.
- Port validator passes: no `import` from `adapters/` inside `core/` or `ports/`.
- Schema round-trip test (if `migration` tag): up-down-up produces identical schema dump.
- Secret-scan clean (no keys in diff).
- OpenAPI schema is valid and unchanged (or changes are in a dedicated `api-change` ticket).

**Fail action:** PR marked draft; agent fixes and re-runs. No human review until green.

---

## Gate 5 — Code review

**Purpose:** an independent pair of eyes.

**Owner:** A second agent OR a human. Clinical-safety tickets require a human; see Gate 6.

**Pass criteria:**
- At least one `Approved` review by a non-author.
- All review comments addressed (either fixed or explicitly deferred to a follow-up ticket).
- Reviewer has verified: acceptance criteria met, tests cover the changes, documentation updated.

**Fail action:** PR remains open with `Changes Requested`. Author iterates.

---

## Gate 6 — Conditional gates (any that apply)

### 6a. Clinical-safety gate

**Triggered by:** tag `clinical-safety`. Applies to any ticket implementing CS-1..CS-12 or touching extraction-to-clinical promotion.

**Owner:** Clinical Reviewer (human clinician from `RACI.md`)

**Pass criteria:**
- Clinical Reviewer has written `CLINICAL APPROVED — <name>, <date>` in the PR thread.
- If edits were made after clinical review, re-approval is required.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge. No override.

### 6b. Integration gate

**Triggered by:** tag `integration`. Applies to any ticket that:
- Modifies files under `web/`, or
- Modifies existing Edge Functions in `supabase/functions/` (including `process-document`), or
- Applies DIS migrations to the live Supabase database, or
- Adds any reference to DIS from existing registration / prescription-pad / generate-prescription flows.

**Owner:** Integration Gatekeeper (user — Dr. Lokender Goyal)

**Pass criteria:**
- Integration Gatekeeper has written `INTEGRATION APPROVED — <name>, <date>` in the PR thread.
- The approval explicitly states what is being integrated.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge. No override. No integration ticket is auto-executable.

### 6c. Security gate

**Triggered by:** tag `security`. Applies to auth changes, secret handling, RLS policy changes, any network-boundary changes.

**Owner:** Security Reviewer

**Pass criteria:**
- Security Reviewer has run `/security-review` and resolved any HIGH/CRITICAL findings.
- CI secret-scan is clean.
- No credentials in logs, error messages, or commit history.

**Fail action:** PR cannot merge.

### 6d. Breaking-change gate

**Triggered by:** tag `breaking`. Applies to port interface changes, schema breaks, API contract breaks.

**Owner:** Architect

**Pass criteria:**
- An ADR exists in `02_architecture/adrs/NNNN-title.md`.
- All consumers are updated in the same PR OR are on a named follow-up ticket list.
- Architect has written `BREAKING APPROVED` in the PR thread.

---

## Gate 7 — Definition of Done

**Purpose:** final pre-merge checklist.

**Owner:** Author (self-check) + final reviewer (cross-check)

**Checklist:**
- [ ] All acceptance criteria checked off with evidence linked (test names, screenshots, log excerpts).
- [ ] TDD updated if architecture changed.
- [ ] OpenAPI updated if API changed.
- [ ] Runbook updated if operational surface changed.
- [ ] `ROADMAP.md` / ticket board updated with `Done`.
- [ ] No TODO / FIXME / `console.log` in production code paths.
- [ ] Changelog entry added (`dis/CHANGELOG.md`).
- [ ] Audit log entry added for migration tickets.

**Fail action:** PR reopened; author addresses gaps.

---

## Merge mechanics

- Merge method: **squash-and-merge** for feature tickets; **rebase-and-merge** for migrations (so each migration is one commit). No regular merges except between agent branches and `feat/dis-plan`/development branches (per `windows-parallel-agents` orchestrator flow).
- The Architect is the only role that can merge to the main integration branch.
- Branch naming: `feat/dis-<agent-id>` for agent work; `feat/dis-###-<slug>` for implementation tickets.

## Emergency override

There is **no emergency override** for Gates 6a (clinical-safety) or 6b
(integration). If the situation is truly urgent, escalate to SEV1 and
follow `09_runbooks/incident_response.md` — that path has its own
authority model and explicit post-hoc review requirement.

# Ticket Board — Document Ingestion Service

This folder is the agentic execution backlog. Every piece of work lives
as a ticket. The Architect (Claude orchestrator) creates tickets;
worker agents execute them under the review gates defined in
`08_team/review_gates.md`.

## Layout

```
07_tickets/
├── README.md                  (this file)
├── epics.md                   (A..H — high-level groupings)
├── backlog.md                 (DIS-### tickets, full text)
├── in_progress.md             (what's currently being worked on)
├── done.md                    (completed tickets; append-only log)
├── blocked.md                 (waiting on clarification / dependencies)
├── integration_hold.md        (tickets gated on user integration approval)
└── clarifications/
    └── CLAR-###.md            (one file per open clarification)
```

## Ticket lifecycle

```
Drafted (Architect)
   │
   ▼
Ready   (Gate 1 passed — pre-start)
   │
   ▼
In Progress (Test-first committed — Gate 2 passed)
   │
   ├── → Blocked (dependency / clarification)
   │       │
   │       └── → Ready (once unblocked)
   │
   ▼
In Review (PR open, Gates 4 + 5 running)
   │
   ▼
Conditional Review (Gate 6 — safety / integration / security / breaking)
   │
   ▼
Done (Gate 7 — DoD checked, merged)
```

## Ticket ID scheme

- `DIS-###` — sequential, never reused.
- `CLAR-###` — clarifications.
- `ADR-###` — architecture decision records (under `02_architecture/adrs/`).

## Tag reference

| Tag | Meaning | Special gate |
|-----|---------|---------------|
| `core` | Changes to `dis/src/core/` or `dis/src/ports/` | — |
| `adapter` | Changes inside `dis/src/adapters/` | — |
| `ui` | Changes to verification UI (new files under `dis/ui/`) | — |
| `migration` | SQL migration | Gate 6d (breaking) if destructive |
| `test` | Test-only ticket | Still requires Gate 4 + 5 |
| `doc-only` | Documentation / runbook | Skips Gate 2 (test-first) |
| `clinical-safety` | Implements CS-1..CS-12 | Gate 6a (clinical reviewer) |
| `integration` | **Touches existing system** (web/, existing Edge Functions, live schema) | **Gate 6b — user approval required** |
| `security` | Auth / secrets / RLS | Gate 6c |
| `breaking` | Port interface or schema break | Gate 6d |
| `infra` | CI, deploy, secrets, monitoring | — |

## The integration hold rule (binding)

**No ticket in `integration_hold.md` may be pulled into `in_progress` without
an explicit `INTEGRATION APPROVED` note from the Integration Gatekeeper
(Dr. Lokender Goyal) in the ticket thread.**

This is the enforcement of the "no integration until we say so" rule.
Tickets tagged `integration` are parked in `integration_hold.md` as soon
as they are drafted. Agents cannot pick them up.

## Working an agent wave

1. Architect selects N tickets that are `Ready` and have no unmet dependencies.
2. Architect ensures none are in `integration_hold.md`.
3. Architect pre-installs any shared deps (per the
   `windows-parallel-agents` skill's orchestrator flow, step 1).
4. Architect creates one worktree per selected ticket (step 2 of the skill).
5. Architect dispatches agents with the v3 hardened prefix + ticket brief.
6. Architect merges agent branches sequentially after verification.
7. Architect updates `done.md` and moves dependent tickets to `Ready`.

## Ownership of this board

The Architect owns the backlog. Worker agents do NOT edit `epics.md`,
`backlog.md`, or the status lists — they only touch files inside
`dis/` per their ticket brief. Status transitions happen when the
Architect merges their branch.

# Epics

Each epic is a coherent slice of work with its own acceptance outcome.
Tickets live under one epic. Epics do not cross the integration gate
unless they explicitly say so.

## Dependency graph

```
A (Foundations) ──► B (Core + Ports) ──► C (Adapters) ──► D (Orchestration)
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                                         E (Verification UI)
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                              F (Observability + Safety audits)
                                                              │
                                                              ▼
                                            ┌──── G (Integration) [HELD — user gate]
                                            │
                                            ▼
                                    H (AWS Port dry-run)
```

Epics A–F are fully executable by agents without touching the existing
system. Epic G is held behind the integration gate. Epic H validates
portability on AWS sandbox.

---

## Epic A — Foundations

**Goal:** the skeleton of the service builds, tests pass, nothing does
anything useful yet.

# Ticket Board — Document Ingestion Service

This folder is the agentic execution backlog. Every piece of work lives
as a ticket. The Architect (Claude orchestrator) creates tickets;
worker agents execute them under the review gates defined in
`08_team/review_gates.md`.

## Layout

```
07_tickets/
├── README.md                  (this file)
├── epics.md                   (A..H — high-level groupings)
├── backlog.md                 (DIS-### tickets, full text)
├── in_progress.md             (what's currently being worked on)
├── done.md                    (completed tickets; append-only log)
├── blocked.md                 (waiting on clarification / dependencies)
├── integration_hold.md        (tickets gated on user integration approval)
└── clarifications/
    └── CLAR-###.md            (one file per open clarification)
```

## Ticket lifecycle

```
Drafted (Architect)
   │
   ▼
Ready   (Gate 1 passed — pre-start)
   │
   ▼
In Progress (Test-first committed — Gate 2 passed)
   │
   ├── → Blocked (dependency / clarification)
   │       │
   │       └── → Ready (once unblocked)
   │
   ▼
In Review (PR open, Gates 4 + 5 running)
   │
   ▼
Conditional Review (Gate 6 — safety / integration / security / breaking)
   │
   ▼
Done (Gate 7 — DoD checked, merged)
```

## Ticket ID scheme

- `DIS-###` — sequential, never reused.
- `CLAR-###` — clarifications.
- `ADR-###` — architecture decision records (under `02_architecture/adrs/`).

## Tag reference

| Tag | Meaning | Special gate |
|-----|---------|---------------|
| `core` | Changes to `dis/src/core/` or `dis/src/ports/` | — |
| `adapter` | Changes inside `dis/src/adapters/` | — |
| `ui` | Changes to verification UI (new files under `dis/ui/`) | — |
| `migration` | SQL migration | Gate 6d (breaking) if destructive |
| `test` | Test-only ticket | Still requires Gate 4 + 5 |
| `doc-only` | Documentation / runbook | Skips Gate 2 (test-first) |
| `clinical-safety` | Implements CS-1..CS-12 | Gate 6a (clinical reviewer) |
| `integration` | **Touches existing system** (web/, existing Edge Functions, live schema) | **Gate 6b — user approval required** |
| `security` | Auth / secrets / RLS | Gate 6c |
| `breaking` | Port interface or schema break | Gate 6d |
| `infra` | CI, deploy, secrets, monitoring | — |

## The integration hold rule (binding)

**No ticket in `integration_hold.md` may be pulled into `in_progress` without
an explicit `INTEGRATION APPROVED` note from the Integration Gatekeeper
(Dr. Lokender Goyal) in the ticket thread.**

This is the enforcement of the "no integration until we say so" rule.
Tickets tagged `integration` are parked in `integration_hold.md` as soon
as they are drafted. Agents cannot pick them up.

## Working an agent wave

1. Architect selects N tickets that are `Ready` and have no unmet dependencies.
2. Architect ensures none are in `integration_hold.md`.
3. Architect pre-installs any shared deps (per the
   `windows-parallel-agents` skill's orchestrator flow, step 1).
4. Architect creates one worktree per selected ticket (step 2 of the skill).
5. Architect dispatches agents with the v3 hardened prefix + ticket brief.
6. Architect merges agent branches sequentially after verification.
7. Architect updates `done.md` and moves dependent tickets to `Ready`.

## Ownership of this board

The Architect owns the backlog. Worker agents do NOT edit `epics.md`,
`backlog.md`, or the status lists — they only touch files inside
`dis/` per their ticket brief. Status transitions happen when the
Architect merges their branch.
